answer.evidence: The booth is a flat front view. Two side pillars frame a blue back wall, and a 3-row blue strip at rows 16-18 sits at the top with a light line at row 19. That strip has no eave shadow and no roof or awning plane, so it reads as a front-facing lintel. The pillars are plain vertical strips with no tops. The counter has a small top band (rows 26-30, lightest edge line at row 30), but it is a secondary part. The main structure has no roof or top surface, and the width profile is a constant 32 px for rows 15-33, then 20-26 px with no widening or narrowing that would suggest a roof.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny desk/booth prop (blue frame, monitor, red chair) about one tile in size. It has no roof, no walls and no door, so it is not a whole building and does not match the reference kind. The measured facts (20 visible tones, 7% near-flat, 0% neutral dark edges) look fine for a small object, and the outline is tinted, but that is not enough. The reference buildings show 5-6 shaded steps per material, with scalloped roof tiles, plaster speckle and individually shaded stones. The candidate has about 3 steps per material (blue frame, red chair, brown desk), and its large areas are simple fills. As a building it is far less rich and complete than either reference, and at this scale it reads as a sticker-like icon rather than a Beodeul-quality structure.
